sanskrit: evam uktas tu bharato niṣādādhipatiṃ guham pratyuvāca mahāprājño vākyaṃ hetvarthasaṃhitam
english: Thus addressed, Bharata, of great wisdom, replied to Guha, the lord of the Niṣādas, with words bearing reasoned meaning.

sanskrit: ūrjitaḥ khalu te kāmaḥ kṛto mama guroḥ sakhe yo me tvam īdṛśīṃ senām eko 'bhyarcitum icchasi
english: "Your wish is indeed noble, O friend of my elder, that you alone desire to honour such an army of mine."

sanskrit: ity uktvā tu mahātejā guhaṃ vacanam uttamam abravīd bharataḥ śrīmān niṣādādhipatiṃ punaḥ
english: Having said this, the glorious Bharata, of great splendour, again spoke excellent words to Guha, lord of the Niṣādas.

sanskrit: katareṇa gamiṣyāmi bharadvājāśramaṃ guha gahano 'yaṃ bhṛśaṃ deśo gaṅgānūpo duratyayaḥ
english: "By which route shall I go to the āśrama of Bharadvāja, O Guha? This region along the Gaṅgā is very dense and difficult to cross."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ guho gahanagocaraḥ
english: Hearing those words of the wise prince, Guha, who ranged the forest depths, spoke with joined palms.

sanskrit: dāśās tv anugamiṣyanti dhanvinaḥ susamāhitāḥ ahaṃ cānugamiṣyāmi rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
english: "Skilled archers among our fishermen shall accompany you, O prince of great renown, and I too shall accompany you."

sanskrit: kaccin na duṣṭo vrajasi rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaḥ iyaṃ te mahatī senā śaṅkāṃ janayatīva me
english: "Surely you do not march with ill intent toward Rāma, whose deeds are faultless? This great army of yours raises a suspicion in me."

sanskrit: tam evam abhibhāṣantam ākāśa iva nirmalaḥ bharataḥ ślakṣṇayā vācā guhaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: To him speaking thus, Bharata, pure as the sky, replied to Guha with gentle words.

sanskrit: mā bhūt sa kālo yat kaṣṭaṃ na māṃ śaṅkitum arhasi rāghavaḥ sa hi me bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ pitṛsamo mama
english: "May such a dreadful time never come! You ought not to suspect me — for that Rāghava is my elder brother, equal to a father for me."

sanskrit: taṃ nivartayituṃ yāmi kākutsthaṃ vanavāsinam buddhir anyā na te kāryā guha satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: "I go to bring back Kākutstha who dwells in the forest. You should entertain no other thought, O Guha — I speak truth to you."

sanskrit: sa tu saṃhṛṣṭavadanaḥ śrutvā bharatabhāṣitam punar evābravīd vākyaṃ bharataṃ prati harṣitaḥ
english: He, with face beaming with joy on hearing Bharata's words, spoke again to Bharata, filled with delight.

sanskrit: dhanyas tvaṃ na tvayā tulyaṃ paśyāmi jagatītale ayatnād āgataṃ rājyaṃ yas tvaṃ tyaktum ihecchasi
english: "Blessed are you! I see none on earth equal to you, who willingly wish to renounce a kingdom that has come to you without effort."

sanskrit: śāśvatī khalu te kīrtir lokān anucariṣyati yas tvaṃ kṛcchragataṃ rāmaṃ pratyānayitum icchasi
english: "Undying fame shall surely follow you through the worlds, you who desire to bring back Rāma from his affliction."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇasya guhasya bharataṃ tadā babhau naṣṭaprabhaḥ sūryo rajanī cābhyavartata
english: While Guha was conversing thus with Bharata, the sun lost its lustre and night drew on.

sanskrit: saṃniveśya sa tāṃ senāṃ guhena paritoṣitaḥ śatrughnena saha śrīmāñ śayanaṃ punar āgamat
english: Having encamped the army, gratified by Guha, the glorious one returned to his bed together with Śatrughna.

sanskrit: rāmacintāmayaḥ śoko bharatasya mahātmanaḥ upasthito hy anarhasya dharmaprekṣasya tādṛśaḥ
english: Such grief, born entirely of longing for Rāma, beset the great-souled Bharata — one undeserving of it, ever mindful of righteousness.

sanskrit: antardāhena dahanaḥ saṃtāpayati rāghavam vanadāhābhisaṃtaptaṃ gūḍho 'gnir iva pādapam
english: Grief burned the Rāghava with an inner fire, scorching him as a hidden flame scorches a tree consumed in a forest fire.

sanskrit: prasrutaḥ sarvagātrebhyaḥ svedaḥ śokāgnisaṃbhavaḥ yathā sūryāṃśusaṃtapto himavān prasruto himam
english: Sweat born of the fire of grief poured from every limb, as the Himālaya, heated by the sun's rays, pours forth its snow-melt.

sanskrit: dhyānanirdaraśailena viniḥśvasitadhātunā dainyapādapasaṃghena śokāyāsādhiśṛṅgiṇā
english: With brooding meditation as its cliffs, sighs as its minerals, a thicket of dejection as its trees, and the fatigue of grief as its lofty peaks —

sanskrit: pramohānantasattvena saṃtāpauṣadhiveṇunā ākrānto duḥkhaśailena mahatā kaikayīsutaḥ
english: — its living creatures the boundless stupefactions, its bamboos the anguish of affliction — by such a great mountain of sorrow was the son of Kaikeyī overwhelmed.

sanskrit: guhena sārdhaṃ bharataḥ samāgato mahānubhāvaḥ sajanaḥ samāhitaḥ sudurmanās taṃ bharataṃ tadā punar guhaḥ samāśvāsayad agrajaṃ prati
english: The great-souled Bharata, who had come together with Guha, collected in mind yet deeply despondent — Guha then comforted that Bharata once more concerning his elder brother.

sanskrit: ācacakṣe 'tha sadbhāvaṃ lakṣmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ bharatāyāprameyāya guho gahanagocaraḥ
english: Then Guha, who ranged the forest depths, described to the immeasurable Bharata the true conduct of the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ jāgrataṃ guṇair yuktaṃ varacāpeṣudhāriṇam bhrātṛ guptyartham atyantam ahaṃ lakṣmaṇam abravam
english: "I spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who was keeping vigil, endowed with virtues, bearing a choice bow and quiver, wholly intent on guarding his brother."

sanskrit: iyaṃ tāta sukhā śayyā tvadartham upakalpitā pratyāśvasihi śeṣvāsyāṃ sukhaṃ rāghavanandana
english: "'This comfortable bed has been prepared for you, dear one; rest and sleep upon it at ease, O joy of the Rāghava clan.'"

sanskrit: ucito 'yaṃ janaḥ sarve duḥkhānāṃ tvaṃ sukhocitaḥ dharmātmaṃs tasya guptyarthaṃ jāgariṣyāmahe vayam
english: "'All these people are accustomed to hardship; you are fit for comfort, O righteous one. We shall keep watch for his protection.'"

sanskrit: na hi rāmāt priyataro mamāsti bhuvi kaś cana motsuko bhūr bravīmy etad apy asatyaṃ tavāgrataḥ
english: "'There is none on earth dearer to me than Rāma. I am not carried away by eagerness — even if I speak this, it is not untruth before you.'"

sanskrit: asya prasādād āśaṃse loke 'smin sumahad yaśaḥ dharmāvāptiṃ ca vipulām arthāvāptiṃ ca kevalām
english: "'Through his grace I hope for great renown in this world, abundant attainment of righteousness, and wealth entire.'"

sanskrit: so 'haṃ priyasakhaṃ rāmaṃ śayānaṃ saha sītayā rakṣiṣyāmi dhanuṣpāṇiḥ sarvaiḥ svair jñātibhiḥ saha
english: "'Therefore I shall guard Rāma, dear friend, as he sleeps with Sītā, bow in hand, together with all my own kinsmen.'"

sanskrit: na hi me 'viditaṃ kiṃ cid vane 'smiṃś carataḥ sadā caturaṅgaṃ hy api balaṃ prasahema vayaṃ yudhi
english: "'Nothing is unknown to me who always roam this forest; we could withstand even a fourfold army in battle.'"

sanskrit: evam asmābhir uktena lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā anunītā vayaṃ sarve dharmam evānupaśyatā
english: "Thus spoken to by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, ever mindful of righteousness, all of us were persuaded."

sanskrit: kathaṃ dāśarathau bhūmau śayāne saha sītayā śakyā nidrāmayā labdhuṃ jīvitaṃ vā sukhāni vā
english: "'How can sleep be obtained, or life, or pleasures, while the son of Daśaratha lies on the ground with Sītā?'"

sanskrit: yo na devāsuraiḥ sarvaiḥ śakyaḥ prasahituṃ yudhi taṃ paśya guha saṃviṣṭaṃ tṛṇeṣu saha sītayā
english: "'He who cannot be withstood in battle by all the gods and asuras together — see him, O Guha, lying on the grass with Sītā!'"

sanskrit: mahatā tapasā labdho vividhaiś ca pariśramaiḥ eko daśarathasyaiṣa putraḥ sadṛśalakṣaṇaḥ
english: "'This one son of Daśaratha, possessed of fitting marks, was obtained through great austerity and manifold hardship.'"

sanskrit: asmin pravrājite rājā na ciraṃ vartayiṣyati vidhavā medinī nūnaṃ kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati
english: "'With him banished, the king will not endure long; the earth will swiftly become a widow.'"

sanskrit: vinadya sumahānādaṃ śrameṇoparatāḥ striyaḥ nirghoṣoparataṃ nūnam adya rājaniveśanam
english: "'The women, exhausted and weeping with loud lament, have surely fallen silent — the royal palace is devoid of sound today.'"

sanskrit: kausalyā caiva rājā ca tathaiva jananī mama nāśaṃse yadi te sarve jīveyuḥ śarvarīm imām
english: "'I do not expect that Kausalyā, or the king, or my own mother, will all survive this night.'"

sanskrit: jīved api hi me mātā śatrughnasyānvavekṣayā duḥkhitā yā tu kausalyā vīrasūr vinaśiṣyati
english: "'My mother might survive, sustained by care for Śatrughna; but Kausalyā, who bore a hero, being afflicted, will perish.'"

sanskrit: atikrāntam atikrāntam anavāpya manoratham rājye rāmam anikṣipya pitā me vinaśiṣyati
english: "'It is all over, utterly over — without attaining his heart's desire, without installing Rāma on the throne, my father will perish.'"

sanskrit: siddhārthāḥ pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ tasmin kāle hy upasthite pretakāryeṣu sarveṣu saṃskariṣyanti bhūmipam
english: "'Those whose purposes have been fulfilled will, when that time arrives, perform all the funeral rites and cremate the king.'"

sanskrit: ramyacatvarasaṃsthānāṃ suvibhaktamahāpathām harmyaprāsādasaṃpannāṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitām
english: "'With its pleasant squares and courtyards, its well-laid broad highways, its palaces and mansions, adorned with all manner of gems —'

sanskrit: gajāśvarathasaṃbādhāṃ tūryanādavināditām sarvakalyāṇasaṃpūrṇāṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākulām
english: "'— thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots, resonant with the sounds of musical instruments, filled with every auspiciousness, crowded with joyful and prosperous people —'

sanskrit: ārāmodyānasaṃpūrṇāṃ samājotsavaśālinīm sukhitā vicariṣyanti rājadhānīṃ pitur mama
english: "'— full of groves and pleasure gardens, graced with assemblies and festivals — in my father's royal city they will roam happily.'"

sanskrit: api satyapratijñena sārdhaṃ kuśalinā vayam nivṛtte samaye hy asmin sukhitāḥ praviśemahi
english: "'May we also, together with the one true to his vow and in good health, enter it joyfully when this time has passed.'"

sanskrit: paridevayamānasya tasyaivaṃ sumahātmanaḥ tiṣṭhato rājaputrasya śarvarī sātyavartata
english: "While the great-souled prince stood there lamenting thus, the night passed away."

sanskrit: prabhāte vimale sūrye kārayitvā jaṭā ubhau asmin bhāgīrathītīre sukhaṃ saṃtāritau mayā
english: "At dawn, when the sun shone clear, after having both of them form their matted locks, I ferried them across with ease at this bank of the Bhāgīrathī."

sanskrit: jaṭādharau tau drumacīravāsasau mahābalau kuñjarayūthapopamau vareṣucāpāsidharau paraṃtapau vyavekṣamāṇau saha sītayā gatau
english: "The two mighty ones, scorchers of foes, wearing matted locks and bark garments, bearing choice quivers, bows, and swords, resembling bull elephants of the herd, went forth scanning the way with Sītā."

sanskrit: guhasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bharato bhṛśam apriyam dhyānaṃ jagāma tatraiva yatra tac chrutam apriyam
english: Having heard Guha's most painful words, Bharata fell into a stupor right there, at the very spot where the painful account was heard.

sanskrit: sukumāro mahāsattvaḥ siṃhaskandho mahābhujaḥ puṇḍarīka viśālākṣas taruṇaḥ priyadarśanaḥ
english: Tender-limbed, of great inner strength, lion-shouldered, long-armed, with eyes broad as a lotus, youthful and pleasant to behold —

sanskrit: pratyāśvasya muhūrtaṃ tu kālaṃ paramadurmanāḥ papāta sahasā totrair hṛdi viddha iva dvipaḥ
english: — having regained consciousness for but a moment, then utterly despondent, he fell suddenly, like an elephant struck to the heart with a goad.

sanskrit: tadavasthaṃ tu bharataṃ śatrughno 'nantarasthitaḥ pariṣvajya rurodoccair visaṃjñaḥ śokakarśitaḥ
english: Śatrughna, who stood close beside him, embracing Bharata in that state, wept aloud, beside himself and emaciated by grief.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāḥ samāpetur mātaro bharatasya tāḥ upavāsa kṛśā dīnā bhartṛvyasanakarśitāḥ
english: Then all the mothers of Bharata rushed forward — thin from fasting, wretched, worn out by the misfortune of their husband.

sanskrit: tāś ca taṃ patitaṃ bhūmau rudantyaḥ paryavārayan kausalyā tv anusṛtyainaṃ durmanāḥ pariṣasvaje
english: They gathered weeping around him as he lay fallen on the ground; and Kausalyā, following after, despondent, embraced him.

sanskrit: vatsalā svaṃ yathā vatsam upagūhya tapasvinī paripapraccha bharataṃ rudantī śokalālasā
english: The devoted, sorrow-worn woman held him as a cow holds her calf, and weeping, consumed by grief, questioned Bharata.

sanskrit: putravyādhir na te kaccic charīraṃ paribādhate adya rājakulasyāsya tvadadhīnaṃ hi jīvitam
english: "Does not the affliction of your sons oppress your body, dear child? The life of this royal family depends on you today."

sanskrit: tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā putra jīvāmi rāme sabhrātṛke gate vṛtte daśarathe rājñi nātha ekas tvam adya naḥ
english: "Seeing you, my son, I live — with Rāma and his brother gone, with King Daśaratha departed, you alone are our protector today."

sanskrit: kaccin na lakṣmaṇe putra śrutaṃ te kiṃ cid apriyam putra vā hy ekaputrāyāḥ sahabhārye vanaṃ gate
english: "Have you heard something untoward regarding Lakṣmaṇa, dear child? Or regarding the only son of her who has gone to the forest with his wife?"

sanskrit: sa muhūrtaṃ samāśvasya rudann eva mahāyaśāḥ kausalyāṃ parisāntvyedaṃ guhaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He, of great renown, having composed himself for a moment though still weeping, consoled Kausalyā and then spoke these words to Guha.

sanskrit: bhrātā me kvāvasad rātriṃ kva sītā kva ca lakṣmaṇaḥ asvapac chayane kasmin kiṃ bhuktvā guha śaṃsa me
english: "Where did my brother pass the night? Where were Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa? On what bed did he sleep? What did he eat? Tell me, Guha."

sanskrit: so 'bravīd bharataṃ pṛṣṭo niṣādādhipatir guhaḥ yad vidhaṃ pratipede ca rāme priyahite 'tithau
english: Thus questioned, Guha, lord of the Niṣādas, told Bharata what he had done when Rāma came as a beloved and honoured guest.

sanskrit: annam uccāvacaṃ bhakṣyāḥ phalāni vividhāni ca rāmāyābhyavahārārthaṃ bahucopahṛtaṃ mayā
english: "Food of various kinds, delicacies, and diverse fruits were abundantly brought by me for Rāma's meal."

sanskrit: tat sarvaṃ pratyanujñāsīd rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ na hi tat pratyagṛhṇāt sa kṣatradharmam anusmaran
english: "Rāma of true valour declined all of it; indeed he did not accept it, bearing in mind the duty of a kṣatriya."

sanskrit: na hy asmābhiḥ pratigrāhyaṃ sakhe deyaṃ tu sarvadā iti tena vayaṃ rājann anunītā mahātmanā
english: "'For us it is not fitting to receive, O friend; it is always our part to give' — thus were we counselled by that great-souled one, O king."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena samānītaṃ pītvā vāri mahāyaśāḥ aupavāsyaṃ tadākārṣīd rāghavaḥ saha sītayā
english: "Having drunk water fetched by Lakṣmaṇa, the great and glorious Rāghava observed a fast that night together with Sītā."

sanskrit: tatas tu jalaśeṣeṇa lakṣmaṇo 'py akarot tadā vāg yatās te trayaḥ saṃdhyām upāsata samāhitāḥ
english: "Then Lakṣmaṇa also performed his rite with the remaining water; those three, with restrained speech, attended the twilight devotions with full concentration."

sanskrit: saumitris tu tataḥ paścād akarot svāstaraṃ śubham svayam ānīya barhīṃṣi kṣipraṃ rāghava kāraṇāt
english: "After that, Saumitri made an auspicious bed, having himself quickly brought kuśa grass for the sake of Rāghava."

sanskrit: tasmin samāviśad rāmaḥ svāstare saha sītayā prakṣālya ca tayoḥ pādāv apacakrāma lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "Rāma lay down on that bed together with Sītā; and Lakṣmaṇa, having washed their feet, withdrew."

sanskrit: etat tad iṅgudīmūlam idam eva ca tat tṛṇam yasmin rāmaś ca sītā ca rātriṃ tāṃ śayitāv ubhau
english: "This is that iṅgudī tree's root, and this is that very grass on which Rāma and Sītā both lay that night."

sanskrit: niyamya pṛṣṭhe tu talāṅgulitravāñ śaraiḥ supūrṇāv iṣudhī paraṃtapaḥ mahad dhanuḥ sajyam upohya lakṣmaṇo niśām atiṣṭhat parito 'sya kevalam
english: "Having fastened his finger-guard and arm-guard, with his two quivers full of arrows, the scorcher of foes Lakṣmaṇa strung his great bow and stood the whole night through, going around him alone on all sides."

sanskrit: tatas tv ahaṃ cottamabāṇacāpadhṛk sthito 'bhavaṃ tatra sa yatra lakṣmaṇaḥ atandribhir jñātibhir āttakārmukair mahendrakalpaṃ paripālayaṃs tadā
english: "And I too, bearing a choice bow and arrows, took my stand there where Lakṣmaṇa stood, guarding him who resembles great Indra, together with my kinsmen who were vigilant and had taken up their bows."
